title: Finding a coach and a shooting ground on ClayArena
summary: What the ClayArena catalogues of coaches and shooting grounds show, how to use them and what to ask before your first visit.

body.html: Many shooters begin with a coach, who sees faults from the outside and corrects them before they become habits. How to choose a coach: First lessons and choosing a coach.

The ClayArena coach catalogue can be filtered by discipline, country, federation and training language. A coach's card shows the disciplines they teach and the languages they speak. It often shows the price too, or says “by agreement”. From the card you can open the coach's full profile.
Training language matters. If you and the coach have no common language, you can work with an interpreter or agree on a few key words in advance: Training with a coach who speaks another language.
The shooting grounds catalogue shows grounds as a list and on a map. A ground's page usually tells you which disciplines it offers, where it is, how to contact it and which competitions it hosts.
Before your first visit, contact the ground and ask a few questions:

html: Can a beginner come, and is there an instructor or a coach?
Can you hire a gun and buy cartridges on site?
Which disciplines and layouts are open that day?
What should you bring: glasses, hearing protection, documents?

body.html: If a competition is coming up at that ground, ask when you may practise. The two disciplines have different rules:

html.sporting: Before the event nobody may practise on the competition layouts (the stands and targets set up for the competition). You can train on the ground's other layouts.
html.compak: You may practise on the competition trajectories (the flight paths the targets will follow in the competition), but with a different setting table. This is the plan that says which traps are shot from each station, as singles or doubles. So in practice the targets do not come in the same combinations as on competition day. At continental and world championships, official practice opens on the Saturday before the event.

body.html: Planning to train at a ground in another country? Check in advance the rules for bringing a gun and cartridges, or ask the ground whether you can hire a gun there. More in Travelling with a gun inside the EU and Outside the EU: national permits.
ClayArena is also preparing training tours with a coach, called ClayAway. They are being prepared and have not launched yet: Travelling with a coach on a ClayAway tour.

key_points.html: The coach catalogue can be filtered by discipline, country, federation and language.
The grounds catalogue shows grounds as a list and on a map.
Before a first visit, ask about beginners, gun hire and what to bring.
Practice before a competition: not on the competition layouts in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™; with other setting tables in Compak® Sporting.
Before training abroad, check the rules for bringing a gun.

did_you_know.html: In both disciplines nobody may coach a competitor during the competition, that is, give them tips or signals. If the referee sees it, the shooter gets a yellow card, and the referee sends the person coaching out of the shooting area. So work with your coach before and after the event.

quiz.q: What can you filter the ClayArena coach catalogue by?
quiz.explain: You can filter by discipline, country, federation and training language.

quiz.q: A Sporting™ competition takes place at your ground next week. Where may you practise before it?
quiz.explain: In Sporting™ nobody may practise on the competition layouts before the event.

quiz.q: Your coach has come to watch your competition. What may the coach do while you shoot?
quiz.explain: Coaching during the competition is not allowed in either discipline: it brings a yellow card.
